(At Present Lodged In Dist. Jail, Chittorgarh)
 ----Appellant  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Sohani Kumari W/o Sh. Gopi Singh @ Gopi Lal Rawat, R/o  Payari, Tehsil Badi Sadari, Dist. Chittorgarh.
----Respondents For Appellant(s) : Mr. Dharmendra Singh Gaur For Respondent(s) : Mr. Saleem Khan, PP  Mr. Rajendra Singh Chouhan  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 16/05/2024

The instant appeal has been filed under Section 14A SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act on behalf of the appellant, who is in custody in connection with F.I.R. No.55/2024 registered at Police Station Badi Sadari, Dist. Chittorgarh, for the offences under Sections 363,
366A, 376 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w)(1)(ii) and 3(2)
(v) of the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, against the order dated 15.04.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases,
Chittorgarh whereby, the bail application preferred under Section 439 Cr.P.C. on behalf of the appellant was rejected.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
[2024:RJ-JD:22166] (2 of 3) [CRLAS-631/2024] Leaned counsel for the appellant submitted that the prosecutrix is a mature married woman.

Learned counsel submitted that the prosecutrix, out of her own free will and volition, eloped with the present appellant on 19.02.2024 and travelled with Rahim Khan vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:22166) on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35773679/
1 him to various places.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel submitted that the appellant who is aged about 18 years was having a consensual relationship with the prosecutrix and however, on the relations between them tuning strained, the appellant has been roped in a false criminal case.
Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the appellant is in custody; investigation has already been completed; challan has been filed and trial of the case will take sufficiently long time to be concluded, therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-appellant.
Per Contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submitted looking to the seriousness of the allegations against the present appellant, he does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.

However, learned counsel for the complainant submitted that during pendency of the present bail application, parties have entered into a compromise and have decided to settle their dispute amicably in the spirit of Lok Adalat and therefore, he has no objection in case the appellant is enlarged on bail.

Having regard to the entirety of facts and circumstances as available on record and upon a consideration of the arguments advanced at Bar, this Court prima facie finds sufficient force in the argument of the learned counsel for the appellant that the prosecutrix is a mature married woman and was having a consensual [2024:RJ-JD:22166] (3 of 3) [CRLAS-631/2024] relationship with the present appellant, had voluntarily eloped with the appellant out of her own free will and volition,
cannot be brushed aside at this stage.

This Court also prima facie finds that investigation against the appellant has already been completed and the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the appellant influencing the prosecution witness or tampering with the evidence or fleeing away from justice, in case he is enlarged on bail.
Consequently, the instant appeal is allowed.

The impugned order dated 15.04.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases,
Chittorgarh is set aside.

Special Judge Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases,
Chittorgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is ordered that the accused- appellant Rahim Khan S/o Sh. Sharif Khan Pathan arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.55/2024 registered at Police Station Badi Sadari, Dist.
Chittorgarh shall be released on bail; provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- and two surety bonds of Rs. 25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court with the stipulation to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 666-divya/-
